absent: Although it uses 'response-ability', decolonial authors (Santos, Mignolo) and PAR are absent; power is handled through psychology and organisation theory rather than political economy.
forYou: Pereira et al. (2020) and Charli-Joseph et al. (2023) come from the same 'Pathways' network as Ely et al. (2020) in your project: a direct thread to your extraction-loss evidence.
method: References from Crossref; strands and narrative by Claude, grounded only in the reference list and title.
narrative: The unexpected root is psychotherapy: Berne's transactional analysis (1958) and Karpman's drama triangle (1968). The paper reads sustainability discourse as a drama of victims, rescuers and persecutors, and TD processes as prone to the same roles.

The way out comes from the relational turn: Haraway's 'Staying with the trouble' (2016), Barad (2007) and Bozalek's 'response-ability' in higher education (2023), joined to recent 'relational paradigm' work in sustainability science (Walsh; West).

It sits inside the mainstream TD canon (Lang 2012; Norström 2020; Lawrence 2022) and the inner-transformation strand (O'Brien; Woiwode; Wamsler). Pereira's transformative spaces and Charli-Joseph's Xochimilco work link it to the Pathways network in your project.
